summary_en: Presents an active-perception framework for 3D reconstruction of small underwater targets from multi-directional forward-looking multibeam-sonar images. The method closes the loop between reconstruction quality and AUV scanning-path selection, triggers new views from sparse preliminary geometry, and incrementally fuses sonar-derived point clouds. Simulation and water-tank measurements validate improved reconstruction coverage and efficiency, making it directly relevant to computational acoustic imaging and sonar-based 3D reconstruction.

summary_en: Develops a high-resolution 2.5D underwater mapping method using only a single imaging sonar. The approach forms an acoustic mosaic from 2D sonar imagery and exploits target-shadow geometry to estimate height, compensating for the missing elevation dimension without requiring a multi-sensor 3D sonar setup. The method targets low-visibility and spatially confined environments and is a direct match for computational acoustic imaging and sonar reconstruction.
